correctness.rationale: For fixed known N≥3, M∈{1,…,N−1}, c=a−b>0, the distinct-draw factorial moments yield u=b+cp, v=−c²p(1−p)/(N−1), w=2c³p(1−p)(1−2p)/((N−1)(N−2)). The normalized ratio (N−2)w/(2√(N−1)(−v)^(3/2))=(1−2p)/√(p(1−p)) is a strict decreasing bijection; positive c, then a,b, reconstruct uniquely, including p=1/2 and M=1,N−1. Exchangeability means the first three cross moments determine the entire Bernoulli-triple law, proving exact feasibility. M=1 vs N−1 with c=1/4,u=1/2 yields identical complete two-result laws but opposite w. Independently enumerated all ordered triples, latent configurations and reported vectors with rational probabilities for 54 models (N=3..8, all M, two interior assay pairs), verifying every moment identity. Finite tests corroborate; unlimited N follows from factorial algebra.
